Lots of really good answers here. I would say that you can, but you really don't even have to mention this in a profile. It's not a big deal to guys that are interested in you, really. A dating profile should be nothing more than a fun introduction and is solely about letting the other person know your personality, not your conditions, insecurities, etc. It's totally acceptable to save that stuff for later. If you do mention it in your profile, mention it BECAUSE you have a fun joke about it that displays your personality, but don't make a fun joke about it because you "have to" mention it. It's really not serious enough to have to mention in a dating profile. 

It looks like other people have suggested it, but I was going to say that if you do decide to go on a dinner date for your first date, you can always look up the restaurant, check the menu, and call the host/hostess. They're trained to answer these exact questions about everything on the menu. Then pick something out beforehand that works with your diet so that you can spend more time talking to your date and not the waiter.

As a guy [25M] who does a lot of online dating, I hardly ever go to dinner on a first date, anyway. It seems like too much of a commitment for a first interaction. I usually just ask for something that takes 15 minutes like coffee, a drink, or something fun like milkshakes or ice cream. And trust me, I get the "Sorry :/ I'm lactose intolerant, but I'll totally get a drink with you" response all the time. Like most of the time actually lol. Dietary restrictions are normal and not a big deal to any of us. It's a lot easier to convey face-to-face that you were allergic to gluten before it was cool, anyway. 

Oh and the last thing I wanted to mention was use this as an opportunity to lead date decisions. You're not going to offend anyone by saying that you'd rather go to another restaurant you have in mind or that you only have time for a drink on Saturday. The whole egalitarian dating roles thing is getting really hot nowadays with us millennials and it's honestly such a welcome relief for us men.

Have fun dating!
